sentences.text: Limaysaurus was a medium-sized sauropod dinosaur.
Gregory S. Paul estimated in 2010 that this animal reached a length of 15 meters and a weight of seven tonnes.
Its back featured very tall neural spines that were simple and straight, resembling the letter 'I' rather than being V-shaped.
Unlike the pencil-shaped teeth of Diplodocus, Limaysaurus possessed curved teeth.
Gastroliths have been found in Limaysaurus fossils, suggesting they used them to help grind food in their stomachs.
The holotype specimen is 80% complete and is considered one of the most complete Cretaceous sauropods found in South America.
Limaysaurus fossils were discovered 15 km southwest of Villa El Chocón in Neuquén Province, Patagonia, Argentina.
The holotype specimen was found in 1988 by Lieto Francisco Tessone.

The genus name Limaysaurus comes from the Río Limay river, and the species name tessonei honors the discoverer Lieto Tessone, with the genus formally named in 2004 by Salgado, Garrido, Cocca, and Cocca.
Limaysaurus shared its habitat with Andesaurus and Giganotosaurus in an environment of plains with large, shallow lagoons.
The climate in the habitat of Limaysaurus was mild and humid.
The phylogenetic relationship between Limaysaurus and African sauropods supports the theory of a land bridge connecting South America and Africa 100 million years ago.
Limaysaurus is classified in the family Rebbachisauridae.
Rebbachisaurids, the family of Limaysaurus, form a basal clade within the Diplodocimorpha.
The geological beds containing Limaysaurus date from the Aptian-Albian interval.
There is a debate regarding the age of the formations containing Limaysaurus, with recent studies re-dating them from the Late Cretaceous Cenomanian to the Early Cretaceous Albian.
